cards.prose: Matthew has to stop and say he did not mean bread but *the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees* (Matthew 16:12). Luke names it before anyone can mistake it, *which is hypocrisy*, and says it to his disciples first while a crowd presses so close they tread on one another. Leaven works unseen through the whole lump, and here it is a teaching that looks like one thing and is another.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew gives the warning against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, which the disciples first take for talk about bread.

cards.prose: Matthew sets the saying where the Pharisees have just called his work the work of Beelzebub. Luke sets it among his disciples, after *he that denieth me before men shall be denied before the angels of Elohim (God)* (Luke 12:9) and before the promise that the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) will teach them what to say. In both, a word against the Son of Adam is forgiven and the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) is not.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew gives the saying that every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven men except blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit).

cards.prose: Matthew's lord *called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods*. Luke's servant is one of that kind, one who *knew his lord’s will* and did not make ready or do it, and he *shall be beaten with many stripes*. Luke adds the measure, *unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required* (Luke 12:48). These are servants of the house, judged by what they did with what they were given.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew shows the lord going into a far country and putting his goods into the hands of his own servants.
